related_questions.question: How many days should I wait before taking a COVID test?
related_questions.snippet: If you were exposed to someone who has COVID-19 and you do not have symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after your exposure before testing. If you test too early, you may have an inaccurate result. If you are in certain high-risk settings, you may need to test as part of a screening testing program.

related_questions.question: How soon after exposure is a COVID test positive?
related_questions.snippet: It can take almost a week after exposure to COVID-19 to have a positive test result. If you are fully vaccinated, you should wait three to five days after exposure before getting a test. Evidence suggests that testing tends to be less accurate within three days of exposure.

related_questions.question: What are the FDA guidelines for Covid testing?
related_questions.snippet: To be confident you do not have COVID-19, FDA recommends 2 negative antigen tests for individuals with symptoms or 3 antigen tests for those without symptoms, performed 48 hours apart. A single NAAT test can be used to confirm an antigen test result.
